author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Core Stoic primary text. Foundation of the entire curriculum.

author: Epictetus
notes: Most systematic Stoic teaching on the dichotomy of control.

author: Epictetus
notes: The handbook. Distillation of the Discourses.

author: Seneca
notes: 124 letters. Most readable Stoic primary text. Core to PHIL 701.

author: Seneca
notes: De Brevitate Vitae. Single most-cited Stoic text on time and attention.

author: Plato
notes: Foundation of Western philosophy of virtue and justice.

author: Plato
notes: The examined life. Socrates as the model of philosophical courage.

author: Aristotle
notes: Eudaimonia, virtue as habit, the doctrine of the mean. Essential counterpoint to Stoicism.

author: Cicero
notes: On duties. Best Latin bridge between Greek Stoicism and Roman practice.

author: Cicero
notes: On death, pain, grief, emotional disturbance. Deep Stoic treatment.

author: Musonius Rufus
notes: Cora Lutz translation (1947) via Wikisource. 21 extant lectures. Epictetus was his student. NOTE: Wikisource is paginated by lecture — fetch requires per-lecture scraping, not a single Gutenberg URL.

author: Chrysippus
notes: Via Long & Sedley SVF. Modern scholarship — summary ingestion only via admin corpus page.

author: Plutarch
notes: Moralia. Important Stoic-adjacent treatment of virtue and emotion.

author: Plutarch
notes: De Tranquillitate Animi. Direct treatment of euthymia.

author: Epicurus
notes: Letter to Menoeceus, Herodotus, Pythocles. Important contrast tradition — ataraxia vs Stoic eudaimonia.

author: Pierre Hadot
work: Philosophy as a Way of Life
notes: Modern scholarship — summary ingestion only. Foundational for Arete's approach.

author: Pierre Hadot
notes: Modern scholarship — summary ingestion only. Best commentary on Marcus Aurelius.

author: Cleanthes
notes: Only complete text from the early Stoa. 40 lines. Clearest statement of Stoic theology and the logos.

author: Diogenes Laertius
work: Lives of the Eminent Philosophers Book VII
notes: Primary source for Zeno, Cleanthes, Chrysippus doctrines. Without this, early Stoa is a black hole.

author: Confucius
notes: Legge translation. Eastern virtue ethics — ren, li, junzi.

author: Laozi
notes: Legge translation. Wu wei as counterpoint to Stoic action.

author: Sun Tzu
notes: Giles translation. Strategy and discipline.

author: Michel de Montaigne
notes: Cotton translation. The examined life in practice. Bridge between ancient and modern.

author: Adam Smith
notes: Sympathy, the impartial spectator. Stoic-influenced moral philosophy.

author: John Sellars
notes: Modern scholarship — summary ingestion only. Best introductory overview.

author: Zeno of Citium
notes: Via Diogenes Laertius Book VII. Founder of Stoicism — thin but important.
